title: React 19 Server Actions for AI Workflows
description: Use React 19 Server Actions to invoke .NET backend AI endpoints directly from forms, with automatic error handling and optimistic updates.

data.text: Server Actions: Bridging Client and Server for AI Calls

React 19 introduced Server Actions as a first-class feature. Server Actions are async functions that execute on the server and can be called directly from client components. They serialize form data, handle errors gracefully, and integrate with React's pending state for loading indicators. For AI workflows, this means your chat form can invoke a .NET backend endpoint that streams LLM responses — all without writing a single fetch call.

data.text: Server Action Implementation in Next.js App Router

Server Actions in the App Router are defined with the 'use server' directive. They run in the Node.js server context where they have full access to .NET backend services via HTTP calls to your ASP.NET Core API.

data.text: Server Actions automatically surface errors through React's error boundaries and useFormStatus. The pending state provides real-time feedback without additional boilerplate. For AI applications, this is crucial — users need immediate feedback that their request was received and is being processed.

Use the useActionState hook to track AI action results declaratively. It returns [state, formAction, isPending] and handles serialization/deserialization of form data automatically. Perfect for tool call results that need to update the UI.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Server Actions eliminate manual fetch boilerplate for AI endpoint calls
useOptimistic provides immediate UI feedback before the server responds
useFormStatus exposes pending state for loading indicators
Server Actions integrate with React error boundaries for clean error handling
Perfect for Server-Sent Events streaming from .NET backend to React UI
data.takeaway: Server Actions in React 19 turn AI backend calls into declarative, type-safe, and optimistic-first interactions with zero fetch boilerplate.
